articles.title: Bye bye boys! The provocative reason so many parents now only want girls
articles.summary: Stuart Brazell had already given birth to two boys when she convinced her husband to try for a third baby — certain that this time she'd finally have the dau...
articles.body:
Stuart Brazell had already given birth to two boys when she convinced her husband to try for a third baby — certain that this time she'd finally have the daughter she'd always dreamed of.

Brazell envisioned the little girl so vividly that during sound baths, she imagined them running together through a lavender field.

But when she learned she was expecting another son, the Los Angeles mom was devastated.

"I just sobbed and sobbed and sobbed," Brazell recalled.

She filmed her emotional reaction and later shared it on TikTok, joining other parents publicly documenting their disappointment when the gender-reveal confetti turns blue .

Three years later, she adores her boys, now 8, 6 and 3. Her youngest, she told The Post, is "the best thing that's ever happened to her" and even has an uncanny resemblance to the daughter she once dreamed of.

"But I'll never get the opportunity and privilege to raise a daughter and have that special bond I had with my mother," she admitted, even as she felt blessed to conceive naturally in her 40s.

"I will forever mourn not having a daughter. I think about it daily. Multiple times a day. I cry about it regularly."

Brazell's complicated feelings are part of a larger conversation about "gender disappointment," increasingly playing out at elaborate baby reveals that send expectant parents into tears — and their reactions rack up millions of views on TikTok .

Once considered the coveted family heir and the one to carry the family name, baby boys are getting a decidedly less warm reception in some corners of modern parenthood.

Amid fraught conversations about masculinity , gender roles and the challenges of raising sons, research suggests the age-old preference for boys may be losing its grip.

Until 2011, research consistently found that when asked, most people preferred to have a son. But a 2018 Cornell University study suggested that the longstanding preference for boys was declining.

"It's being driven by a social-media and media generated narrative about toxic masculinity that's become pervasive and self-perpetuating, but that's really not grounded in biological fact," Heidi Murkoff, author of "What to Expect When You're Expecting," told The Post.

Yet the numbers are increasingly looking pink.

A 2025 Gallup International survey of nearly 45,000 people across 44 countries found that 19% of women preferred a daughter, compared with just 12% who wanted a son — though roughly two-thirds had no preference.

The preference has even surfaced in adoption decisions, where studies showed prospective parents favoring girls so strongly that the preference equated to a $16,000 difference in adoption costs.

And some fertility doctors say they're seeing it firsthand.

Dr. Brian Levine, of CCRM Fertility of New York, told The Post he's anecdotally observed an increase in patients seeking daughters through IVF .

"Much of this uptick in my practice has been driven by international patients traveling to the U.S. for their fertility care because sex selection is highly restricted globally for non-medical reasons," Levine said.

For Ruthy Jungreis, a mother of four daughters, the apparent reversal is striking.

When she was having children, friends and relatives would practically offer condolences whenever she welcomed another girl, reassuring her that a son would eventually come along.

But Jungreis, who never had a boy, told the Post she wouldn't have it any other way.

Her four daughters grew up sharing the same interests, from movies to family vacations, and remain incredibly close — a bond she believes might have looked different had she raised sons.

Her daughter Gayil Jungreis, 29, of New York City, has an even stronger opinion and admitted to having gender disappointment when she found her first was a son .

"Parents need at least one daughter, but I don't think they 'need' a son," she told The Post.

Gayil, who grew up with three sisters, believes daughters are the glue that holds families together — particularly as children grow up, marry and start families of their own.

"In general, girls keep a family close and together," she said, adding that she believes daughters make relationships with grandchildren and in-laws easier to navigate.

For some mothers, the longing for a daughter isn't simply about raising a little girl — it's about the lifelong relationship they imagine sharing with her.

But is the baby-boy backlash really as widespread as social media makes it seem?

Among What to Expect's community of roughly 15 million expecting and new moms, candid conversations about gender disappointment are common — but Murkoff told The Post she hasn't seen a discernible anti-boy skew.

"Much more often, any disappointment is over parents discovering that they're expecting another baby of the same gender — the 3rd boy, or the 4th girl," she explained. "Or the disappointment of older kids who had their hearts set on a baby sister, only to bite into a blue cupcake. Cue the tears."

"I'm more concerned that media is fueling negative perceptions that aren't based in reality," she continued. "Every boy is different, and every girl is different. Birth order has an influence, so does personality."

But understanding gender disappointment may require looking beyond the initial reaction.

"Gender disappointment isn't really about the baby being a boy or a girl. It's about letting go of a future you've pictured for yourself," Giulia P. Davis, a licensed marriage and family therapist, told The Post.

Murkoff also cautions against making presumptions that women and girls are better than men and boys.

"Yes, men aren't born to be nurturing, but neither are women — that's a combination of nurture, but also nature.

"Expecting and new fathers experience a surge in estrogen and a drop of testosterone — they produce oxytocin, just as moms do, when snuggling skin to skin with their babies. That's nature at work — for me, that's a much more powerful influence than any male-bashing social media narratives."

For Bret Green, a 39-year-old Nashville dad raising a young son and daughter, the growing negativity surrounding boys misses an important opportunity.

He understands why women who've had difficult experiences with men might feel apprehensive about raising sons. But rather than fearing what their boys might become, he believes parents have a chance to shape a better generation of men.

"Recently I have seen more women showing their disappointment when it's a boy," Green told The Post. "I see having a son as an opportunity to course correct," Green told The Post. "My son can be one of the good ones. That's my responsibility and my wife's responsibility."

Brazell feels that responsibility, too — even if raising three rambunctious boys sometimes resembles a nightly wrestling match.

They've accidentally broken her nose and even damaged her surgically corrected eyesight.

But beneath the roughhousing, she insists, her boys are "so full of love."

"I do think it's interesting that now that people are preferring girls, or this idea that girls are easier to raise," she said, adding that she thinks people may find girls more convenient.

"They're too loud, they're too much. It's a bigger challenge to raise fine young gentlemen. That's a challenge to you to bring wonderful men into this world."

articles.title: Watch: Hot oil spills on 3 as woman rams SUV into kebab centre in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Woman driver gets police notice after SUV rams Bengaluru kebab centre near Bannerghatta; hot oil spill injures three, damages bikes; compensation dispute.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Police have issued a notice to a woman who, on October 28, rammed her SUV into an eatery near Bannerghatta, injuring three men.According to an FIR registered with Bannerghatta police, the Mitsubishi Pajero Sport was driven by Sajina Begum, wife of Safrulla Abdul Aziz, a businessman hailing from Keralam and resident of Electronics City Phase I.In her statement, Begum told cops that she felt giddy when the vehicle came near ‘Halevuru kebab centre’ on CK Palya Road and, in a state of confusion, pressed the accelerator instead of brakes.Gaining sudden speed, the SUV entered into the kebab centre and rammed into the materials, including a vessel containing hot oil.The oil spilled on worker Basavaraj and customers Munikrishna and Manjesh, causing minor burn injuries. Also, a couple of motorbikes placed outside the kebab centre were damaged. After two days of treatment, the injured men were discharged from the hospital, police said.The complaint was filed by Paramesh A, whose bike was damaged in the mishap.“Soon after the accident, the woman had promised to pay the expenses towards the repair of my motorbike. Also, she promised to look after the medical expenses of the injured; but so far, nothing happened and therefore, I am filing the complaint,” Paramesh said.A senior police officer said Sajina Begum and Safrulla Abdul Aziz were regularly purchasing kebab from the same shop.“That day too, they had come to buy kebab, but the accident took place. Aziz claimed he had paid around Rs 75,000 towards the medical expenses of the injured ones. articles.title: DU professor Sangit Ragi’s office ransacked after row over ‘casteist’ slurs
articles.summary: Delhi University professor Sangit Kumar Ragi’s office was allegedly ransacked after a TV debate caste slur row; protests erupted and police complaints were filed.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The office of Sangit Kumar Ragi, a Delhi University professor, was allegedly ransacked by a group of people Wednesday, a day after his remarks against Samajwadi Party spokesperson Manoj Kaka in a television debate triggered a row over casteist slurs.Videos that have surfaced show a group of people entering the social sciences building on North Campus, where Ragi’s office is. They shouted “haye-haye” and demanded Ragi’s suspension.Some of them allegedly smeared cow dung on the gate of his office, covering the nameplate. They allegedly broke the glass pane on the office door, tore and scattered files and damaged furniture. The videos also showed people smearing cow dung inside the office.DU officials who did not wish to be quoted said the university was yet to file a police complaint. The protesters have filed a police complaint against Ragi.Ragi said he would not file a a police complaint as they were students. He said he believed they were from Samajwadi Party’s student outfit.Speaking to TOI, he said the protesters were angry about his remarks during the TV debate, which he admitted he should not have made.“It was a reaction to a fellow panelist. I am not a politician, and I feel I should have restrained myself and perhaps ignored his comments about me. I have personally apologised to him and also issued an apology online,” he said.The All India Students’ Association (AISA) held a separate protest outside Ragi’s office Wednesday and burnt his effigy. The organisation demanded his resignation over the alleged casteist remarks.In the November 3 TV debate, Ragi and Kaka started arguing during a discussion on remarks by Bageshwar Dham’s Dhirendra Shastri. Videos of the exchange circulated on social media. Ragi was heard using a casteist slur against Kaka, who too had used derogatory language against Ragi.Following the backlash, Ragi issued an apology on X Tuesday evening. He said Kaka had repeatedly made personal attacks against him. His response was aimed at people who use abusive language and not at any community, Ragi said.This, however, is not the first time Ragi has faced criticism over remarks during a television debate.In August, his comments about Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had led to complaints before the university’s vice-chancellor and at Parliament Street police station.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Ethiopia expels 6 Sudan diplomats, orders closure of consulate, reports say
articles.summary: Move comes after Sudan lodged official complaints against Ethiopia, accusing Addis Ababa of supporting the RSF group.
articles.body:
Ethiopia has ordered six Sudanese diplomats to leave the country within 48 hours and closed Sudan’s consulate in the border town of Asosa, according to media reports.

The reports on Tuesday came as tensions between the countries continue to rise, with Sudan accusing Addis Ababa of ⁠supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which is fighting the Sudanese army, while Ethiopia accuses Khartoum of backing rebels in its northern Tigray region.

The allegations and counter-allegations, which both ⁠sides deny, have raised fears that Ethiopia’s and Sudan’s wars could bleed into each other, spawning a broader conflict in the Horn of Africa.

The Reuters news agency, citing a senior Ethiopian official, reported on Tuesday that Ethiopia ordered six staff members of the Sudanese consulate in the border town ⁠of Asosa to leave within 48 hours. It said the official asked not to be named in order to discuss a sensitive diplomatic matter.

The Associated Press news agency also reported the action, citing an Ethiopian intelligence official. It also said a Sudanese official had corroborated the expulsions, adding that Ethiopian authorities had summoned Sudan’s ambassador on Sunday to announce the consulate’s closure.

He said the staff departed on Tuesday evening and spoke on condition of anonymity because he did not want to escalate the diplomatic dispute.

The agency said neither official had provided a specific reason for the ousters.

The expulsions came after ⁠Sudan lodged a complaint against Ethiopia with both the United Nations Security Council and the African Union’s Peace and Security Council on Sunday, accusing Ethiopia of allowing the RSF to use its territory to launch deadly drone attacks against civilian infrastructure in Sudan.

“The Sudanese government remains committed to its right to defend its territory. Nevertheless, it is making ⁠every possible effort to avoid an open war with Ethiopia,” said Amjad Farid, political and foreign affairs adviser for Sudan’s Transitional Sovereign Council.

A direct military confrontation with Addis Ababa would severely strain an already exhausted Sudanese military apparatus, which is still involved in intense battles with the RSF in the southeast of the country.

Addis Ababa denies it supports the RSF in Sudan’s civil war.

The fighting between Sudan’s military and the RSF erupted in 2023 and has since killed tens of thousands of people and displaced more than 14 million people. The civil war has created one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, according to the United Nations.

On Sunday, drone strikes on electricity substations in the northern Sudanese towns of Al-Dabbah and Abu Hamad knocked out power. Sudan’s government and the rights group Emergency Lawyers blamed the RSF.

The wider campaign has disrupted electricity and water supplies and threatened essential medical services.

Ethiopia’s order on the Sudanese diplomats follows its decision to expel 10 Eritrean diplomats and close its embassy in Eritrea on October 1. Eritrea responded by severing diplomatic ties.

Ethiopia also expelled an Egyptian diplomat last month. Relations with Egypt have long been strained over Ethiopia’s massive dam on the Blue Nile, which Cairo fears could threaten its water supplies.

Ethiopia has accused Sudan, Egypt and Eritrea of supporting Tigrayan rebels who launched an offensive against government forces in September. All three countries have denied this.

articles.title: Is Pete Hegseth on his way out? Trump weighs Pentagon leadership after GOP setback
articles.summary: As President Trump evaluates the future of Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth following GOP setbacks in the midterms, internal discussions center around the impacts of the Iran war and potential leadership changes within the Pentagon.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump is considering whether to retain Pete Hegseth as defence secretary after Republicans suffered major losses in the midterm elections, with the Iran war emerging as a possible factor in the administration's internal discussions, CBS News reported citing multiple sources familiar with the matter.Trump has raised the question with advisers and in phone conversations, although he has not made a decision on whether to replace Hegseth, the sources told the outlet. The discussions come as the administration faces questions over the political impact of the US war in Iran.Some White House aides believe senior military officials could also face scrutiny over the election outcome. Adm. Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command, and Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, are among those who could face criticism because of their roles in advising on the Iran war, according to sources cited by CBS News.Vice President JD Vance has directly linked the conflict to the Republican defeat. In a post on X on Wednesday morning, he wrote: "The reason we lost is the war."The possibility of Hegseth leaving the Pentagon has also prompted discussion about potential replacements. Another source told a news organisation that Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is being considered as a possible candidate for the position.The source suggested DeSantis could secure Senate confirmation during the lame-duck period before taking up the defence secretary role after his gubernatorial term ends on January 5.Trump, however, publicly dismissed the prospect of replacing Hegseth when questioned by reporters on Wednesday afternoon. "No, I think he's doing a very good job," the president said.He was also asked whether Hegseth could instead be appointed to the Senate seat expected to become vacant when Tennessee Senator Marsha Blackburn takes office as governor. Trump responded: "I actually think he'd be very popular if he did that," but added that he "haven't heard that at all."The White House has also rejected suggestions that Hegseth's position is under threat. Spokeswoman Anna Kelly said in a statement that Trump "has full confidence in Secretary Hegseth".Kelly also defended the administration's military operations in Iran and Venezuela and praised Hegseth's efforts to reverse what she described as the previous Biden administration's emphasis on "DEI and woke ideology".Hegseth was already facing calls for impeachment from Democrats before the midterm elections. articles.title: Multiple grizzlies may have attacked mother and daughter found dead, Canadian authorities say
articles.summary: More than one grizzly may have been involved in a bear attack that relatives say killed a mother and daughter in Bella Coola along the province’s central coast, British Columbia conservation officials said.
articles.body: More than one grizzly may have been involved in a bear attack that relatives say left a mother and daughter dead in Bella Coola along the province’s central coast, the Conservation Officer Service in British Columbia said. The service’s Inspector Jeff Tyre said in a video message that the second body had been found in a search by Royal Canadian Mounted Police and conservation officers on Tuesday afternoon that followed the discovery of the first set of remains a day earlier. He said it’s “not yet clear if more than one bear was involved,” and any bears captured in the area will be assessed. Family members of art therapist Jenny Balcarras and her daughter, Selah Reed, had reported them missing on Sunday. A fundraiser set up by relative Mary Melissa Smith said Reed was 20, “with her whole life ahead of her,” while Balcarras leaves behind three young adult children, as well as a grandchild. Smith said in the post that Balcarras recently moved to Bella Coola to pursue a new career to start a new chapter in her life. Balcarras left behind a son, two daughters and a grandson who now are “faced with the devastating loss of their mother,” while navigating the financial burden of arranging funeral services, Smith said. The Central Coast Teachers’ Association said on social media that Balcarras had joined their school community as a counselor in August, and she devoted “countless hours to connecting with the students she served and worked closely with teachers and other staff supporting their well-being.” Tyre said efforts to capture the bear or bears involved in the attack continue, and any animals captured by the service will be killed in accordance with provincial guidelines to make sure the public is safe. The attack comes nearly a year after a grizzly attack on a group of 20 elementary school students and teachers in the same area, which left one adult and three children badly hurt. The animal involved in that attack last November was never captured. Kim Titchener, founder of Bear Safety & More Inc. based in Calgary, said she was concerned when she saw reports about the women on Facebook hiking groups. “When I saw that they were missing and in the area that they were missing, my heart just dropped because I just kind of knew this could be a bear attack,” Titchener said. “This community and area have suffered so much last year,” she said, referring to the grizzly attack on schoolchildren. Titchener said she had several day cares and school groups calling her for bear safety training following last year’s attack. Bella Coola is well-known for its large population of grizzly and black bears, and Titchener said it’s common for people in Bella Coola to see bears walking near their homes. Titchener said there have been “concerning pressures” on bear populations in British Columbia because of the loss of habitat, food stress caused by drought and climate change, setting off more conflicts with people. “I don’t know if Bella Coola suffered from any drought issues, but certainly other parts of the province of B.C. did,” she said. Tyre said officers are in regular contact with the nearby Nuxalk Nation and the community in Bella Coola to provide updates, and people should continue to stay away from the west trail area of the Snootka trail system where the attack happened.

articles.title: Fim da chuva? Quinta-feira tem previsão de melhora do tempo no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Ainda há previsão de precipitação em algumas regiões do estado ao longo do dia, segundo a Climatempo Meteorologia.
articles.summary: Ainda há previsão de precipitação em algumas regiões do estado ao longo do dia, segundo a Climatempo Meteorologia.
articles.body:
A chuva deve diminuir no Rio Grande do Sul na quinta-feira (5) com o afastamento do sistema de baixa pressão e a entrada de uma massa de ar frio .

Apesar da melhora gradual, ainda há previsão de precipitação em algumas regiões do estado ao longo do dia.

Durante a madrugada, pode chover de forma fraca a moderada em áreas da Região Metropolitana, do Litoral Norte, da Serra, dos Vales e do Norte gaúcho.

No decorrer da quinta, a instabilidade tende a ficar concentrada na metade Leste , onde há possibilidade de chuviscos e chuva fraca. Também podem ocorrer pancadas moderadas e isoladas em pontos da Costa Doce, da Região Metropolitana e da Serra. Nas demais áreas, o tempo deve permanecer firme.

As temperaturas variam entre 12°C e 28°C . As menores marcas são esperadas em São José dos Ausentes, com cerca de 12°C, e em localidades como Barra do Quaraí, Jaquirana e Criúva, que devem registrar aproximadamente 13°C. Já as máximas mais elevadas podem ser observadas em Iraí, Alpestre, Doutor Maurício Cardoso e Vicente Dutra, onde os termômetros podem alcançar 28°C.

Entre os municípios com maiores volumes de chuva previstos para a quinta-feira estão São Martinho, com acumulado de até 25 milímetros, além de Nonoai, Tupanci do Sul e Santo Expedito do Sul, com cerca de 11 milímetros.

Sexta-feira com amanhecer frio e possibilidade de granizo

Na sexta-feira (6) , a massa de ar frio mantém as temperaturas mais baixas nas primeiras horas do dia . O tempo tende a ficar mais firme em grande parte do estado, mas o extremo Norte pode registrar temporais isolados entre a tarde e a noite, inclusive com chance de granizo .

A previsão indica mínimas entre 8°C e 18°C e máximas que podem chegar a 31°C. As menores temperaturas devem ocorrer em Bom Jesus e Monte Alegre dos Campos, enquanto municípios como Alpestre, Planalto, Iraí e Ametista do Sul podem atingir os maiores valores do dia.

O sábado (7) será marcado pelo retorno mais expressivo da instabilidade , principalmente nas regiões Norte e Nordeste do Estado. Nessas áreas, são esperadas pancadas de chuva acompanhadas de trovoadas, com os maiores volumes previstos justamente no Nordeste gaúcho.

O dia começará com temperaturas baixas, especialmente na Serra. As mínimas devem ficar entre 7°C e 15°C, enquanto as máximas variam de 16°C a 24°C.

Barracão aparece entre os municípios com maior volume de chuva previsto, podendo registrar até 59 milímetros. Também são esperados acumulados elevados em Cacique Doble e São José do Ouro, com 57 milímetros, e em São João da Urtiga, com 51 milímetros.

articles.title: Por que Alasca, Kansas e Mississippi demoram a apurar votos nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Prazos para recebimento de cédulas, votos provisórios e dificuldades logísticas podem adiar a definição de disputas até o fim de novembro.
articles.summary: Alasca, Kansas e Mississippi têm regras específicas para apuração das midterms de 2026, com prazos adicionais para votos pelo correio e cédulas provisórias.
articles.body:
A apuração de votos das eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos, conhecidas como midterms, já acabou na maioria dos estados americanos . Os resultados parciais já representam uma vitória expressiva dos democratas sobre os republicanos, e a diferença ainda pode aumentar porque três estados do país só devem concluir suas votações na próxima semana: Kansas, Mississipi e Alaska .

Embora a maior parte dos votos seja contabilizada nos primeiros dias após a eleição, os números divulgados na noite da última terça-feira (3) ainda são preliminares .

Diferenças nas regras de apuração , prazos para recebimento de cédulas pelo correio e procedimentos de conferência fazem com que a apuração nesses locais avance mais lentamente. Em algumas disputas, o vencedor pode levar semanas.

Os estados precisam concluir a conferência das cédulas, analisar votos provisórios e cumprir os respectivos calendários de certificação. Não existe uma data única para a divulgação dos resultados oficiais em todo o país .

Eleitores fazem fila para votar nas eleições legislativas dos Estados Unidos, em Anchorage, no Alasca, no dia 3 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Lindsey Wasson/AP

Nos próximos dias, os estados continuarão atualizando os resultados à medida que novas células forem processadas.

No Alasca , a próxima atualização está prevista para 10 de novembro, com uma nova rodada em 13 de novembro. A última contagem preliminar deve ocorrer em 18 de novembro, quando também será realizada a apuração pelo sistema de voto preferencial, caso necessária. A certificação está prevista para 25 de novembro.

No Kansas , o prazo para recebimento de cédulas pelo correio termina em 6 de novembro. Os conselhos eleitorais dos condados precisam analisar os votos provisórios até 16 de novembro. A certificação estadual deve ocorrer até 1º de dezembro.

No Mississippi , o prazo para recebimento de votos pelo correio e regularização de cédulas provisórias termina em 10 de novembro. Os condados devem encaminhar os resultados certificados até 13 de novembro. A declaração estadual dos resultados está prevista para 3 de dezembro.

Por que a apuração demora em cada estado?

A extensão territorial e as dificuldades de transporte são os principais fatores de atraso no Alasca. O estado tem comunidades isoladas, e muitas delas não têm acesso por estradas. Isso faz com que o transporte das células seja feito por avião ou barco.

Além disso, em 131 dos mais de 400 distritos eleitorais, os votos são contabilizados manualmente.

O estado também permite que cédulas enviadas por eleitores que vivem no exterior sejam recebidas até 15 dias depois da eleição, desde que tenham sido postadas até o dia da votação.

Em disputas nas quais nenhum candidato obtém mais de 50% dos votos, o Alasca ainda utiliza o sistema de voto preferencial, que prevê a redistribuição das preferências dos eleitores. A contagem oficial desse sistema está prevista para 18 de novembro.

No Kansas, o principal motivo da demora é uma decisão judicial que manteve o prazo adicional de três dias para o recebimento de votos enviados pelo correio. Cédulas postadas até o dia da eleição podem ser contabilizadas se chegarem aos escritórios eleitorais dos condados até a próxima sexta-feira (6).

A análise de votos provisórios também prolonga o processo. Essas cédulas são utilizadas quando há dúvidas sobre a elegibilidade ou a identificação do eleitor e só podem ser contabilizadas depois de examinadas pelos conselhos eleitorais dos condados, que têm até 16 de novembro para concluir o procedimento.

No Mississippi, a demora está relacionada principalmente ao prazo adicional para recebimento de votos enviados pelo correio e à análise de cédulas provisórias. O estado aceita cédulas postadas até o dia da eleição, desde que sejam recebidas pelos escritórios eleitorais dos condados até a próxima terça (10).

Também podem entrar na contagem votos provisórios de eleitores que não apresentaram documento de identificação com foto no dia da votação. Para regularizar essas cédulas, os eleitores têm até 10 de novembro para apresentar um documento válido às autoridades eleitorais.

articles.title: Enem 2026: Fisioterapeuta orienta como prevenir dores durante estudos | G1
articles.standfirst: Alongamentos simples e pausas regulares ajudam a reduzir a sobrecarga muscular e melhorar o bem-estar na preparação para as provas.
articles.summary: Alongamentos simples e pausas regulares ajudam a reduzir a sobrecarga muscular e melhorar o bem-estar na preparação para as provas.
articles.body:
Passar horas seguidas estudando para o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) pode causar dores no pescoço, nas costas e nos braços. Para evitar esses desconfortos durante a preparação para as provas, a coordenadora de fisioterapia da Uninassau, Emanuele Paiva, recomenda a adoção de hábitos simples no dia a dia.

Segundo a especialista, as queixas mais frequentes entre os estudantes estão relacionadas ao longo período na mesma posição , seja lendo, escrevendo ou usando dispositivos eletrônicos. Ela explica que pequenas pausas ao longo do dia ajudam a reduzir a sobrecarga muscular.

"As dicas são alongamentos básicos de extensão de braço e de punho, alongamento da coluna vertebral, bem como a hiperextensão da cervical. Isso ajuda bastante. Fora que o aluno precisa sempre estar dando um intervalo, no mínimo a cada uma hora, para ficar de pé, dar uma volta e liberar a musculatura", orientou Emanuele Paiva.

Enem 2026: especialista ensina exercícios para evitar dores durante horas de estudo — Foto: Reprodução

No vídeo, a fisioterapeuta demonstra exercícios de alongamento que podem ser feitos em casa ou no local de estudos, sem a necessidade de equipamentos.

Entre as orientações estão alongar os braços e os punhos, movimentar o pescoço de forma suave e alongar a coluna. A especialista também recomenda que os estudantes façam pausas de alguns minutos a cada hora de estudo para caminhar e mudar de posição.

articles.summary: Festa Literária Internacional de Pernambuco chega à 21ª edição entre os dias 11 e 15 de novembro, em diferentes pontos do Centro do Recife.
articles.body:
Foto de arquivo da 20ª edição da Festa Literária Internacional de Pernambuco (Fliporto) — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

A 21ª edição da Festa Literária Internacional de Pernambuco (Fliporto) acontece entre os dias 11 e 15 de novembro, no Centro do Recife , com uma programação gratuita que reúne literatura, cultura popular, inovação e tecnologia. As inscrições podem ser feitas na internet.

O evento vai promover debates, lançamentos de livros e performances artísticas, além de um prêmio literário. Entre os autores e artistas participantes, estão o músico Lirinha, o jornalista Edney Silvestre e a escritora Maria Valéria Rezende (veja programação abaixo) .

Com o tema “Raízes em papel, sonhos em bytes”, o festival homenageia o escritor pernambucano Marcus Accioly, que morreu em outubro de 2017. Uma das novidades desta edição é uma parceria com o Rec'n'Play, que terá atividades relacionadas à educação e à tecnologia.

O festival também promove uma ação em conjunto com o Instituto Dom Hélder Câmara (IDHeC). A atividade, intitulada “Dom Helder Câmara, o pensador e filosofo da paz”, propõe uma reflexão sobre literatura, filosofia, espiritualidade, memória histórica, direitos humanos e justiça social.

Também estão previstas as seguintes ações:

Biblioteca Digital de Pernambuco - plataforma digital e aplicativo voltados à preservação, organização e divulgação da produção literária pernambucana;

Museu de Arte de Rua de Pernambuco - iniciativa que pretende conectar artistas, instituições culturais, poder público e sociedade civil para valorizar a arte urbana;

articles.title: Mãe de Marília Mendonça desabafa nos 5 anos da morte da cantora | G1
articles.standfirst: Dona Ruth conta que a filha morreu no dia seguinte do aniversário: 'Morre um pedaço de você'. Marília Mendonça morreu ao 26 anos, em 2021, quando ia cumprir uma agenda de shows em Minas Gerais.
articles.summary: Marília Mendonça morreu ao 26 anos, em 2021, quando ia cumprir uma agenda de shows em Minas Gerais.
articles.body:
Após cinco anos da morte da cantora sertaneja Marília Mendonça, a mãe dela, Dona Ruth, desabafou sobre a falta da filha, que morreu em 5 de novembro de 2021 , em um acidente aéreo em Piedade de Caratinga , em Minas Gerais. Em entrevista à TV Anhanguera, Dona Ruth revelou que a filha morreu no dia seguinte do aniversário e que a ausência da filha é a pior dor do mundo ( veja acima ).

"Em novembro, eu me casei, em novembro eu nasci. Em novembro, inclusive, meu aniversário é dia 4 e eu perdi minha filha dia 5. Significa a pior dor que uma pessoa pode passar na vida. Sinto muita saudade. Silenciou a casa, ela era muito alegre, barulhenta", declarou.

Ruth fala sobre a saudade que sente da filha. "Às vezes, falo que estou com saudade, mas falo para Deus, porque às vezes a dor é tanta. Tem dia que é pior. Morre um pedaço de você. Foi um pedaço de mim, mas ficaram outros. Tinha que cuidar dos que ficaram", conta.

Dona Ruth (à direita) chora ao falar sobre a morte de Marília Mendonça, em Goiania, Goiás — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

A mãe de Marília ressalta o legado deixado pela cantora.

"Ela conseguiu realizar o sonho dela, que era cantar, levar multidões. Todo mundo cantando a música dela. Talvez, não tenha visto o quanto era grande em vida, mas, agora, depois de 5 anos, olha o tamanho do legado. Marília nasceu poetisa, não podia desperdiçar isso"

Dona Ruth exibe o closet com as roupas usadas por Marília Mendonça; cantora morreu há cinco anos, em um acidente aéreo — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

Na casa em que Dona Ruth mora em Goiânia , ela mostrou o quarto da filha, que mantém intacto. Nele, estão diversas roupas que Marília usava em shows.

Além das roupas, a mãe guarda ainda uma sanfona, um presente dos cantores sertanejos César Menotti e Fabiano para Marília. Segundo Ruth, ela entra no quarto todos os dias.

Marília Mendonça morreu ao 26 anos, na sexta-feira, dia 5 de novembro de 2021, quando ia cumprir uma agenda de shows em Minas Gerais. Antes do embarque, a cantora publicou em suas redes sociais entrando na aeronave, com a legenda: “Fim de semana de shows em Minas Gerais”.

No post, ela mostrou itens típicos da região mineira, como cachaça, queijo e pão de queijo. Além disso, ela publicou imagens almoçando dentro da aeronave. O avião em que ela embarcou caiu em Piedade de Caratinga, em Minas Gerais.

Ao se aproximar para o pouso, a aeronave atingiu cabos de uma linha de transmissão de energia elétrica, perdeu o controle e caiu em uma área de cachoeira. No avião, também estavam o tio de Marília, Abicieli Silveira Dias Filho, o produtor Henrique Ribeiro, o piloto Geraldo Martins de Medeiros Júnior e o copiloto Tarciso Pessoa Viana.

O velório no Ginásio Goiânia Arena e o enterro da cantora no Parque Memorial atraíram milhares de fãs. Sertanejos também estiveram nas homenagens à Marília, como Henrique e Juliano , Maiara e Maraisa, e o ex-companheiro da cantora e pai do filho dela Murillo Huff. Familiares, amigos, famosos e fãs acompanharam o caixão no carro dos bombeiros durante o cortejo até o cemitério Parque Memorial.

articles.title: O formato do bumbum não revela níveis de hormônios, apesar do que dizem nas redes sociais | G1
articles.standfirst: Na verdade, são os genes, os ossos e os músculos que determinam o formato do seu bumbum, e os hormônios só passam a ter influência gradualmente, por volta da menopausa
articles.summary: Na verdade, são os genes, os ossos e os músculos que determinam o formato do seu bumbum, e os hormônios só passam a ter influência gradualmente, por volta da menopausa
articles.body:
O formato do seu bumbum não diz nada sobre seus hormônios , por mais que algumas postagens recentes nas redes sociais afirmem o contrário. A única maneira de descobrir seus níveis de cortisol, estrogênio ou qualquer outro hormônio é por meio de um exame de sangue.

Um bumbum em formato de coração, dizem algumas influenciadoras, indicaria níveis saudáveis de estrogênio, enquanto um formato em H significaria excesso de cortisol. Na realidade, no entanto, o formato das nádegas não reflete seus níveis hormonais circulantes de um dia para o outro , de uma semana para a outra ou mesmo de um mês para o outro.

Então, o que determina o formato do bumbum? Principalmente seus genes. Eles determinam sua estrutura esquelética e o tamanho e a estrutura dos seus músculos. E, nas nádegas e em todas as outras partes do corpo, a quantidade de gordura que você provavelmente acumulará nessas áreas.

O formato da pelve varia de pessoa para pessoa . Na obstetrícia, quatro categorias tradicionais descrevem a estrutura óssea interna da pelve, que também corresponde ao formato da abertura pela qual o bebê passa durante o parto: ginecóide, andróide, antropoide e platipeloide.

A forma ginecóide é a mais comum nas mulheres e a mais favorável para um parto vaginal. A forma andróide é mais estreita e se assemelha à forma da pelve masculina. A forma antropoide é mais estreita lateralmente, mas mais longa na direção da frente para trás, enquanto a forma platipeloide apresenta o inverso. Não é possível determinar qual tipo uma mulher possui apenas observando a pele sobre a pelve ou as nádegas.

Essa estrutura óssea é à qual seus músculos se ligam. Ela também determina os espaços ao redor deles que são preenchidos com gordura. Quase todas as características que você pode ver ou medir nos quadris e nas nádegas derivam dessa arquitetura óssea. Em outras palavras, seu esqueleto define o ponto de partida.

Por cima fica a pele, que revela os contornos do tecido subjacente. Isso dá origem aos tipos de nádegas frequentemente descritos por cirurgiões plásticos: em forma de H, A, O e V invertido.

O sulco abaixo de cada nádega, conhecido como prega infraglútea, se forma onde a pele e os tecidos subjacentes se ligam a estruturas mais profundas. Essas ligações ajudam a determinar a posição e o formato da borda inferior das nádegas.

Os músculos também contribuem para o formato das nádegas, e essa é a parte que você pode alterar mais facilmente. Algumas pessoas que perdem uma quantidade significativa de peso ao tomar medicamentos à base de GLP-1 desenvolvem o que é conhecido como “bumbum Ozempic”, em que as nádegas parecem mais achatadas ou flácidas. Isso pode refletir a perda de gordura e músculo, bem como alterações na pele.

O formato das nádegas realmente muda mais tarde na vida das mulheres. Isso geralmente está relacionado à menopausa, quando os níveis de estrogênio começam a diminuir. À medida que o estrogênio diminui, a gordura é depositada na região abdominal em vez de sob a pele ao redor dos quadris e das nádegas, como ocorre antes da menopausa. Portanto, os hormônios realmente influenciam onde a gordura se acumula, mas apenas como parte de uma mudança lenta e de longo prazo.

Isso não significa que uma mulher passe de um formato de nádegas para outro — a genética não muda. Qualquer mudança de curto prazo ao longo do ciclo menstrual, impulsionada pelos ritmos hormonais, provavelmente será imperceptível. Isso se deve à retenção de líquidos, que ocorre em todo o corpo e não em uma região específica.

O esqueleto da mulher também se altera com o envelhecimento na região da menopausa, influenciado pela perda muscular, alterações hormonais e tecidos conjuntivos mais frouxos. Mas esse é um processo de longo prazo.

O estresse também não vai mudar nada. Um período particularmente estressante vai alterar seus níveis de cortisol, mas isso não fará com que a gordura se desloque do bumbum para a barriga. O estresse pode fazer com que mais gordura seja armazenada em uma determinada área, mas é bem conhecido que nossa genética determina onde nossa gordura é armazenada.

Esta não é a primeira vez que as redes sociais tentam convencer as pessoas de que o formato de suas nádegas pode ser alterado. As covinhas nos quadris também já foram apontadas como algo que se pode modificar, mas, assim como as nádegas, seu formato é influenciado principalmente pela genética, que determina nossa estrutura esquelética e muscular.

Mudar qualquer coisa tão dependente da genética geralmente requer cirurgia. E, nessa parte do corpo, certas operações apresentam alguns dos maiores riscos de morte entre as cirurgias estéticas.

O formato das suas nádegas reflete uma combinação de anatomia herdada, gordura e músculos. Os hormônios podem influenciar como esse formato muda com o tempo, principalmente na menopausa, mas a aparência por si só não é suficiente para determinar se seus níveis hormonais estão normais.

articles.title: Após ataque hacker, Binance libera saques de mais criptomoedas | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa diz que depósitos seguem funcionando normalmente.
articles.summary: Empresa diz que depósitos seguem funcionando normalmente.
articles.body:
Logotipo da Binance. — Foto: Dado Ruvic/Reuters

A Binance anunciou que vai ampliar, a partir desta quinta-feira (5), a retomada dos serviços de saque de criptomoedas após o ataque hacker que resultou no roubo de US$ 6,3 bilhões em criptoativos.

Segundo a empresa, as retiradas de dezenas de ativos em diferentes redes começarão a ser liberadas gradualmente a partir das 4h desta quinta-feira, no horário de Brasília.

A corretora ressaltou que os ativos não serão liberados de uma só vez. Cada combinação de criptomoeda e rede terá os saques retomados somente após a conclusão de verificações de segurança.

Entre as redes contempladas nesta nova etapa estão Ethereum (ETH), BNB Smart Chain (BSC), Base, Tron (TRX), Polygon (MATIC) e Sui. Criptoativos como UNI, AAVE, PAXG, FLOKI, SAND, ENS e GRT estão entre os previstos para ter os saques restabelecidos.

Os depósitos, segundo a Binance, continuam funcionando normalmente.

A empresa afirmou que está priorizando os ativos de acordo com a demanda dos usuários registrada na última semana. Outros criptoativos deverão ser acrescentados gradualmente à lista conforme as verificações de segurança forem concluídas.

A Binance também alertou que, durante a retomada, usuários podem enfrentar atrasos ou tempos maiores de processamento. A orientação é consultar o status da rede e de cada ativo antes de tentar fazer uma retirada.

Ataque pode ser o maior roubo financeiro da história

A retomada ocorre depois de a Binance sofrer um ataque hacker que provocou o roubo de US$ 6,3 bilhões em criptoativos e pode ser o maior roubo financeiro da história, segundo a Reuters.

A Binance afirmou nesta terça-feira (3) que os invasores usaram uma falsa entrevista de emprego e computadores comprometidos para chegar aos sistemas da empresa. O ataque culminou no roubo realizado em 29 de outubro.

Segundo um relatório inicial divulgado pela corretora, a invasão começou meses antes. Em junho, um funcionário da equipe responsável pelas carteiras baixou uma ferramenta de inteligência artificial adulterada.

A Binance disse ter detectado o problema, substituído o equipamento e alterado credenciais de acesso. Mesmo assim, segundo a companhia, os invasores conseguiram obter informações sobre as funções desse funcionário e de outros integrantes da equipe.

Em setembro, um segundo engenheiro de software que buscava um novo emprego baixou um repositório de código malicioso após participar de uma entrevista para uma vaga que acreditava ser verdadeira. O processo incluiu uma reunião virtual com o suposto CEO de uma empresa, que na realidade era fictícia.

Em 20 de outubro, de acordo com a Binance, o invasor utilizou o computador comprometido e uma ferramenta interna de inteligência artificial para assumir o controle dos sistemas usados por desenvolvedores da equipe de carteiras.

Nove dias depois, o hacker utilizou credenciais roubadas e executou um script malicioso que deu início ao ataque.

O FBI atribuiu a invasão a um grupo de hackers norte-coreano. A Coreia do Norte rejeitou a acusação.

A Binance afirmou que está ressarcindo os clientes que perderam recursos no ataque e que ampliará os investimentos em sistemas de detecção com uso de inteligência artificial.

“Isso não deveria ter acontecido, e pedimos desculpas pela preocupação, pelos transtornos e pela incerteza que isso causou aos nossos usuários, parceiros e ao setor como um todo”, afirmou a empresa em relatório sobre o caso.

articles.title: Northern Ireland Troubles Bill: No shoot-to-kill missions against IRA, says former SAS officer
articles.summary: The soldier is speaking out now because of the government's draft law to deal with the legacy of the Troubles.
articles.body:
A former officer with the Army's Special Air Service (SAS) has denied it was involved in shoot-to-kill missions against the IRA during the Troubles in Northern Ireland.

George Simm had remained silent about his time in Northern Ireland for almost 50 years, but has now accused the government of abandoning veterans in its legislation to deal with the legacy of the conflict.

He served during the 1970s and 80s and was involved in hundreds of operations, including an SAS ambush in which three IRA men were killed.

The government said the Troubles Bill, which seeks to deal with unresolved legacy of the decades-long violent conflict, "includes effective safeguards for any veteran" .

The special forces unit of the British Army was involved in scores of the most controversial killings during the conflict and while the majority of its victims were IRA members it also killed civilians.

While no official numbers are available for killings carried out by the SAS, according to Simm the unit arrested more people than it killed.

"When you shoot you shoot to kill but the inference from our detractors using propaganda was that you went out there with the full intent to kill, we didn't," he said.

He added the evidence "on every occasion as far as I am aware has proved the opposite".

He said "this is just propaganda" and attacked the "weakness and pathetic nature of the British government to not deal with this".

"They are not fit to be in charge of an army on operations," he added.

The UK government has said it has "strengthened" the proposed legislation to ensure it includes "effective safeguards" for any veteran who is asked to provide information to the Legacy Commission or a coroner.

"It makes clear that there was no equivalence between lawful conduct by soldiers and the actions of terrorists. And in cases relating to the Army the operational context and orders by senior officers must be taken into account," a Northern Ireland Office spokesperson told BBC News NI.

Victims and veterans keeping close watch on Troubles legacy bill debate

Draft law to deal with Troubles legacy backed by MPs

NI Secretary defends planned changes to Troubles bill

Asked if he could recall any incidents when those they shot dead could have been arrested, he said: "No not at all. Two of the ones I was on they were firing at us when we got out of cars, we were under fire.

"We were absolutely professional and highly trained and if your premise is true then every one of the guys we arrested would be dead, so its not true."

George Simm was the SAS commander in charge when his unit killed three IRA men in an ambush at Drumnakilly near Omagh in 1988.

The gang which included brothers Gerard, 29, and Martin Harte, 23, together with their brother-in-law Brian Mullan, 26, had planned to kill an off duty UDR man while he was driving a coal lorry.

But the SAS unit had been tipped off about the attack and were waiting for the gang. Simm posed as the lorry driver and pretended he had broken down at the side of the road.

"I heard the car coming and could see it was a Sierra and suddenly out of the back window was a hood with a gun and he fired a burst at me which forced me to take evasive action," he said.

"The car was speeding towards me and there were bullets flying everywhere and I went around the back of the truck, and I know it was Martin Harte who was firing under the truck.

"I could feel them and the bullets were flying into the hedge where the other guys were and I thought some of them may have been hit but they weren't."

He said the car stopped and one of the other IRA men ran around the back of the truck "to kill him", and then the soldiers opened fire.

He added it was all over in "three or four seconds" and "that was the end of the operation".

The families of the three men have insisted it was a "shoot-to-kill operation" and they could have been arrested.

Ignatius Harte, a brother of two of men, previously told the BBC that the Army had "prior knowledge of the men being armed, they had access to the weapons so therefore they could have been arrested at any time and charged".

"They lured them into an ambush and shot them dead without any warning," he added.

But when asked if it was a "shoot-to-kill mission", George Simm said "definitely no".

"When someone is shooting at you with a Kalashnikov at close range" and bullets are travelling at "600m a second it is not possible to think rationally in a nanosecond".

"We are ready for every operation, so if they shoot or they're intending to shoot us, then we'll go at it," he said.

"But we can also do the other one which is the aim. The police want to get hold of these guys and interrogate them."

Simm said he had been previously questioned at an inquest about the SAS operation at Drumnakilly and had nothing to hide.

The Northern Ireland Troubles Bill replaces the previous Conservative government's contentious 2023 Legacy Act, which introduced a ban on inquests and civil actions related to Troubles-era incidents .

Labour's bill involves a legacy commission to investigate Troubles-related killings, a separate information recovery body, and a dedicated legacy unit within An Garda Síochána (Irish police).

Simm said he was "frustrated" because the narrative around the regiment and the British Army had been "so perverted, so corrupted by stupid politics and the corruption of the legal process".

"So people like me decided we are going to change that as we want people to understand the truth about the operations because that is rarely spoken about as the MoD censor us," he said.

"They tell us you can't talk about it and at the same time they order us into a courtroom to do exactly that. I'm not doing that anymore as I've been abused by their stupidity for too long."

He also questioned why it was only soldiers who appear in a witness box when so many others who were in the chain of command are never called to give evidence.

Asked about the risks of going public and concerns about his personal safety, he said: "I am 72 and I'm just not worried anymore. There is a bigger game in play here and I am duty bound to do what I am doing and its not just me.

"The whole of the SAS association, a great swathe of senior officers finally are in the game and have got into the fight."

The former officer also challenged republicans and said the IRA was now fighting the war by other means.

"They've all put away their weapons in the deep hides and they've all got laptops now and they are all social media warriors doing the same thing but we have to continue to fight, but we need to sort the law out first," he said.

"Families are jumping up and down claiming the British government did this and the SAS did that.

"I would be more inclined to ask the leadership of the republican movement what did they do and for what. Because it was all for nothing."

articles.title: UK interest rates: Bank of England expected to raise them for first time in over three years
articles.summary: Most analysts are predicting an increase from 3.75% to 4%, the first increase in more than three years.
articles.body:
Policymakers at the Bank of England are expected to raise interest rates on Thursday in what would be the first increase to the benchmark rate for more than three years.

Most analysts are predicting an rise from 3.75% to 4% in a move that would increase the cost of borrowing for individuals and businesses, but boost savers.

The Bank rate has fallen from its 2023-24 peak of 5.25%, although the Bank's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has left the rate unchanged at its last six meetings.

Rising inflation, driven primarily by the cost of petrol and diesel, will push policymakers into an interest rate hike, analysts suggest.

The announcement will be made by the Bank at 12:00 GMT on Thursday.

Close attention will also be paid to any hints from the MPC on the future direction of interest rates.

"The decision is increasingly less about whether rates reach 4% and more about what follows after that," said Chris Cheverall, head of UK at trading platform CMC Markets.

"A quarter-point rise is already widely expected, but the Bank now has to balance inflation that is still too high against an economy where the growth outlook has weakened sharply."

The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) measure of inflation is well below its peak of a few years ago but has been heading back up and is expected to go higher.

It was 3.5% in the year to September 2026 , up from 3.1% the previous month and well above the central bank's 2% target.

The ongoing impact of the Iran war, primarily on the cost of energy and fuel, has filtered through to the UK inflation rate. Millions of domestic energy customers are braced for a hefty rise in prices in January.

The Bank of England last raised rates in August 2023.

Its base rate is what it charges other banks and building societies to borrow money, which influences what they charge their own customers for mortgages as well as the interest rate they pay on savings.

Were the Bank rate to rise, there would be an immediate impact on the 510,000 tracker mortgage-holders.

A 0.25 percentage point rise would mean a £31 increase in monthly repayments for someone with a typical tracker home loan, according to calculations by banking trade body UK Finance.

The 470,000 mortgage-holders on variable deals would need to wait for their lender's reaction to any Bank rate rise. Typically, a 0.25 percentage point rise would mean a £14 increase per month in repayments.

The picture for those on fixed deals is more nuanced.

While their monthly payments are not immediately affected by a rate change, their future deals are, and lenders have already "priced in" the expected rate rise when quoting new deals.

As of 4 November, the average two-year fixed residential mortgage rate was 5.96%, while the average five-year rate stood at 5.99%, according to financial information service Moneyfacts.

It means anyone rolling off a five-year deal faces a much bigger mortgage bill.

Broker L&C said that average mortgage rates offered by the 10 biggest lenders suggested some borrowers now faced paying almost £5,000 more each year in repayments on a £200,000 mortgage over 25 years than those who secured a remortgage deal in 2021.

Five years ago, the average five-year fixed remortgage rate among the 10 biggest lenders was 1.30%.

Relatively high fixed rates have prompted some people to consider choosing trackers, in the hope that the rate would be lower, even if the Bank rate rises in the coming months.

"The right choice ultimately depends on borrowers being confident they can stomach future rises. The devil is in the detail," said Rachel Springall from Moneyfacts.

The cost of some other new loans could be influenced by the Bank rate.

Savers, on the flipside, could see the interest rates offered to them improve in light of any rise in the Bank rate.

Ultimately, lenders - as well as policymakers at the Bank of England - are having to judge what may happen to the UK's economic outlook which is highly connected to changes in international events.

articles.body: Three US states were set to carry out executions on Thursday, with Indiana preparing to execute a man convicted of killing two children in a house fire, while Florida and Alabama also scheduled lethal injections, the Associated Press reported.The three executions would mark the second time this year that three people have been put to death on the same day. Indiana, meanwhile, was preparing for its first execution of 2026.Indiana man convicted of killing girlfriend's two childrenJeffrey Weisheit, 50, was convicted of setting a fire that killed his girlfriend's children, aged eight and five, at a home near Evansville in 2010. The killings were apparently linked to the deteriorating relationship between the couple.His lawyers had urged Republican Governor Mike Braun to commute his death sentence to life imprisonment. They also sought permission for Weisheit to undergo brain scans to support claims that he had a history of head injuries and mental health problems. Braun rejected both requests.Weisheit also challenged Indiana's planned use of lethal injection drugs purchased from a pharmacy facing a disciplinary hearing before the state Pharmacy Board. However, the Indiana Department of Correction said it was confident in its ability to carry out the execution humanely.Florida, Alabama also scheduled executionsIn Florida, Jesse Guardado, 64, was scheduled to be executed for fatally stabbing a 75-year-old woman inside her Walton County home in 2004 before stealing her jewellery, cash and other valuables.Guardado had confessed to the killing and pleaded guilty. articles.title: Would you take a test to see if your life will be cut short? I did - and it changed me
articles.summary: Laura Sides faced a dilemma of whether to find out if she would inherit her father's condition.
articles.body:
If you could find out if you had a gene that would cut your life short, would you?

This is the dilemma Laura Sides faced when she was offered a test for the rare form of early onset dementia that her dad was diagnosed with in his 40s.

Laura spoke to Dr Sian Williams, host of BBC Radio 4's Life Changing podcast, about her decision to take the test and how it has shaped the rest of her life.

Growing up, Laura says she always felt close to her dad as they had a "similar nature". He was a GP and "the most amazing doting father," she says. When his Alzheimer's symptoms became more severe, Laura dropped out of university to care for him.

"We did have a really lovely time," she says, remembering trips to a lighthouse and collecting coasters. " I'd run him baths and just play music and pour jugs of hot water over his head and he loved it."

It was at a hospital appointment with her dad when a doctor told Laura she had a 50/50 chance of developing the same type of early onset Alzheimer's known as the "London variant".

"All I could think was, that's a toss of a coin," she says. "I was still so involved with what was going on with him [her dad]. I just pushed it really, really deep down."

Laura's dad died in 2009, just a year after her mum had died.

"All of a sudden I got such an overwhelming urge to leave," she says. So she booked a solo around-the-world trip, eventually settling in Melbourne, Australia.

It was there that thoughts of inheriting her dad's condition "started creeping in" and she went to see a specialist in 2013.

He told her a test could determine with 99.999% certainty if she would inherit early onset dementia. If she had the gene, her expected age of decline would be 46 to 48, he said.

"I just thought, I'm not there yet. I don't want to do that."

As Laura entered her 30s she found herself thinking about the test more and more and decided she wanted to know. But first, she had to undergo six months of genetic counselling.

"There's not many realms in life where you find out your fate and it can be very difficult information to process," she says.

After a six-week wait for the test results to come through, the day finally arrived. Laura says she felt "extremely nervous".

She had booked a table for lunch with a friend afterwards - but went into the appointment alone.

"I said, 'Let's cut straight to it.' They said, 'We're really sorry, it's not good news, and you have inherited the gene.'"

She remembers "almost a white blurry noise of just sitting there".

"I came out of that room and my friend burst into hysterical tears." But Laura didn't react. "We went for our lunch and it was lovely. I don't know if it'd sunk in."

The reality hit later. "I was angry. I felt it was so unjust. I was just too confused at how I was meant to live now. How do you live with that knowledge?"

Laura began to feel a pull back home to the UK, especially as her sister was pregnant. "It doesn't make sense... to live on the other side of the world when she's going to have a baby."

However, her around-the-world travels continued as she took part in medical trials before and after her diagnosis.

"It felt like such a positive to be involved in something out of such a negative situation."

Laura is now 43 - three years away from the age doctors predicted she will begin to notice symptoms.

"I keep waiting for something to sort of hit home. I guess one day I'll start declining but that doesn't keep me up at night."

She is "grateful and so lucky for the people in her life". But meeting anyone new is hard.

"Do I tell them? Do I not tell them? At what point do I tell them?

"And more often than not, when I have told them, it ends."

However she says she has been "proven wrong".

"I have been shown I can be loved despite this. It fills my heart with reassurance and joy".

Laura says she had always "naively assumed" she would be a mother.

"[Its] one of the very few things that I never questioned that I'd be good at and I wanted to do. That's hard... but it doesn't make sense to do it. It wouldn't be fair."

For Laura, life is now about tapping in to things that "make her happy".

"It's not about huge aspirations. It's not like I want to see the Grand Canyon... I want to have time now around the people that I adore and make me feel safe.

"I love nature. I love being outside. I'm obsessed with being submerged in water. It sounds so corny, but...I believe it really is actually the little things are the big things.

"I hope I just have a wonderful few years in this world... drinking champagne and eating oysters - two of my favourite things."

If you or someone you know has been affected by dementia, you can access support from the BBC Action Line.

articles.title: A Connecticut man sought shared custody of a dog after a breakup; an appeals court ruled that the law did not allow the court to order shared possession
articles.summary: A Connecticut man who sought possession of a dog he had shared with his former partner has lost his appeal. In Gaynor v.
articles.body: A Connecticut man who sought possession of a dog he had shared with his former partner has lost his appeal. In Gaynor v. Gilman, officially released on 21 July 2026, the Connecticut Appellate Court affirmed the denial of Alexander Gaynor’s application for a prejudgment remedy of replevin concerning a chihuahua mix named Buzz. According to the Connecticut Appellate Court Judgement, the plain and unambiguous wording of General Statutes § 52-515 does not provide for shared possession of a chattel, and Mr Gaynor did not seek shared possession in his application. The court also held that his claim about proving a superior possessory interest was unreviewable.Why did a Connecticut man seek shared custody of a dog after a breakupThe opinion states that the relationship ended in June 2022 and that Ms Gilman moved out of the shared apartment. The parties decided to continue sharing Buzz, and they did so by regularly exchanging him on mutually agreed dates. According to the opinion, in October 2023, after approximately eighteen months of sharing the dog following the breakup, Ms Gilman unilaterally determined that she would no longer allow Mr Gaynor to see Buzz. The opinion adds that she has kept the dog for herself and that Mr Gaynor, despite repeated demands for the dog's return, has not seen Buzz since.On 22 November 2023, in anticipation of commencing litigation, Mr Gaynor filed an application for a prejudgment remedy. The opinion records that the trial court, Judge Vizcarrondo, held an evidentiary hearing on 23 and 25 July 2024 and heard testimony from seven witnesses, including both parties. At the hearing, Mr Gaynor's counsel agreed with the court that he was claiming a right to immediate possession but was not necessarily seeking exclusive possession, and said that if exclusive possession had to go to one party or the other, he would claim it. The trial court found that the parties' possessory rights in Buzz were equal and denied the application, stating that Buzz is a chattel and not a child. The trial court added that a custody and visitation scheme is provided for in the family context.What does Connecticut law say about shared possession of a dog in replevin casesThe Appellate Court explained that replevin proceedings in Connecticut are governed by statute, namely General Statutes § 52-515. According to the opinion, that section provides that the action of replevin may be maintained to recover goods or chattels in which the plaintiff has a general or special property interest with a right to immediate possession and which are wrongfully detained from him, together with damages for the wrongful detention. The opinion states that the court's role is to interpret statutes as they are written and that it cannot read into them provisions that are not clearly stated.Applying that approach, the Appellate Court concluded that the "plain and unambiguous" wording of § 52-515 does not provide for shared possession of a chattel. The opinion adds that, even if it did, Mr Gaynor's claim as alleged in the verified complaint attached to his application was expressly predicated on § 52-515, and in his prayer for relief he sought a temporary order of replevin ordering possession of Buzz to him until a final resolution of the action, together with damages. According to the opinion, he did not seek shared possession in his application, and a court is not permitted to decide issues outside those raised in the pleadings. The Appellate Court therefore concluded that the only relief the trial court could have afforded, had it found probable cause to sustain the replevin claim, would have been the unqualified possession of Buzz pending a final resolution of the action, along with damages for the unlawful detention.Mr Gaynor's arguments at trial affect his appeal over possession of BuzzMr Gaynor also claimed on appeal that the trial court wrongly required him to show that his possessory interest in Buzz was superior to Ms Gilman's to establish his right to immediate possession. The opinion states that he argued the elements he had to establish derived only from § 52-515 and the Supreme Court's decision in Cornelio v. Stamford Hospital, and that the trial court had instead relied on language from the Appellate Court's decision in Angrave v. Oates. The Appellate Court held that this claim was unreviewable. According to the opinion, before the trial court, Mr Gaynor had claimed that his possessory interest was superior, had cited Angrave in his prehearing memorandum for the proposition that a replevin action involves a comparison of competing rights to possess the animal, and had testified that he had cared for or had possession of Buzz for more days than Ms Gilman. The opinion adds that, when the trial court asked about the superiority of his claim, his counsel responded that he could establish superiority.The Appellate Court concluded that Mr Gaynor had prompted the error he complained of on appeal by suggesting to the trial court in his prehearing memorandum that the question was relevant, by presenting evidence on it and by arguing through counsel that he had proved it. The opinion states that this result is the same whether the matter is called induced error, waiver or abandonment, and that an appellant cannot create a reviewable claim because appellate counsel disagrees with the strategy of trial counsel. The judgment was affirmed, and the other judges concurred. The opinion also records, in a footnote, that Mr Gaynor commenced a separate action against Ms Gilman on 30 July 2024, with claims for breach of contract (replevin), conversion, civil theft and negligent infliction of emotional distress. According to the opinion, that action was tried in March 2026.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology
articles.summary: British diplomats are looking to offer reassurance that there is a sense of urgency to deal with the issue, even if a date for doing so is not yet confirmed, Chris Mason writes.
articles.body:
The UK has signed up to "structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith" talks that address the "historical harms" of the transatlantic slave trade, Commonwealth leaders in Antigua have said.

The formal conclusions marking the end of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, known as the communique, is the joint text setting out what has been agreed.

The 18 page document includes a paragraph in which the leaders "welcome the agreement of the Government of the United Kingdom to engage in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms".

It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham opened the door to a formal apology on behalf of the UK for its role in the slave trade, while ruling out the prospect of reparations.

Officials said the timeframe for the talks would be agreed at a later date, though the Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has suggested they are likely to conclude in around a year.

Asked whether the government might reach the point of a formal apology by the time it hosts the G20 leaders' summit in Manchester next November, Miliband told BBC Newscast : "Broadly speaking, yes."

The rationale among British diplomats in committing to the wording in the communique is to try to offer reassurance that there is a sense of urgency to deal with the issue, even if a date for doing so is not yet confirmed.

This will be determined, sources said, in the "structured dialogue" the UK is promising with countries that have long demanded that the pain and lasting legacies of the slave trade are, as they see it, properly addressed.

Burnham said his "new approach with the Commonwealth" had been "well received" at the summit.

He said it had "been the most successful meeting of the Commonwealth in recent times," adding that "the King's words have resonated powerfully here and we're really pleased with how it's gone".

King Charles III, speaking in his role as Head of the Commonwealth, told the meeting: "The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other Members of our Commonwealth.

"As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow."

articles.title: More asbestos found in Parliament, as MPs urged to get on with revamp
articles.summary: MPs told it's crunch time for a decision on refurbishment amid warnings of a Notre Dame-style fire.
articles.body:
More asbestos has been discovered in Parliament, the BBC has learnt, as MPs come under pressure to sign off on a major revamp of the crumbling home of UK democracy.

Known asbestos items in the Palace of Westminster and wider parliamentary estate, such as insulation, roofing, floor tiles and ropes, now number more than 1,650 - an increase of 500 since 2021.

It comes as the government considers holding a vote on refurbishing Parliament, which could cost up to £40bn and take 61 years, after years of indecision and delay.

The Commons public accounts committee this week warned it was "crunch time" for Parliament's restoration, with every additional year of delay costing taxpayers £420m.

More asbestos items were found during surveys in preparation for the long-awaited refurbishment project, parliamentary authorities said.

Asbestos has been identified as one of the main reasons for the refurbishment, given the dangers to human health when its fibres are airborne. While asbestos is largely fireproof, surrounding fire and heat can release fibres over long distances.

In the past five years, 700 items of asbestos have been removed from Parliament but the total has still risen, a Freedom of Information request by the BBC found.

Under Health and Safety Executive guidelines, most of it is classed as low risk in concealed areas, meaning it is less likely to be disturbed, but almost 200 items are classed as medium risk meaning they may require remedial works.

A spokesperson for UK Parliament said its "absolute priority is the safety of the those who work on and visit the parliamentary estate" with improved asbestos monitoring, new awareness training, and plans to further remove it.

Kris Gledhill, the son of former Labour MP Alice Mahon who died in 2022 of malignant mesothelioma - a type of cancer linked to asbestos exposure - told the BBC "asbestos should never be considered low risk".

"A precautionary approach should be adopted: this includes assessing the fact that in addition to the risks from buildings deteriorating over time, there are also risks of damage from extreme weather events, floods and fire, and from disturbances caused during renovation and maintenance work," he said.

"Alice was well aware of the risks relating to asbestos and mesothelioma," he added.

"She was able to identify two workplaces where she might well have been exposed, one of which was the Palace of Westminster."

The Commons authorities told the BBC "an asbestos-free building cannot be achieved in practice" because that would require demolition or extensive damage to the fabric of the building.

Dr Hannah Moody, chief executive of charity Mesothelioma UK which campaigns on asbestos-related diseases, said she backs introducing a national asbestos register and the phased removal of asbestos from public buildings.

"Although asbestos was banned in 1999, it remains present in many public buildings across the UK and continues to cause serious illness and work-related deaths, including from the aggressive cancer, mesothelioma," she said.

Workers should be given health and safety advice to manage the risks, she added.

The findings come as the Commons Public Accounts Committee on Wednesday published the results of its inquiry into Parliament's restoration and renewal (R&R) programme, which is exploring options to revamp the site.

Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, the Conservative MP who chairs the committee, told the BBC that if a small fire broke out in the building "the whole lot would go up" - with 24-hour fire patrols in place.

"Consider the impact of global rolling news footage of Notre Dame-like flames licking out of the building's roof, resulting in the destruction of our heritage, or worse, injuries or loss of life," he added.

He said this was a "real and rising... grave risk" and criticised "a political allergy to gripping the nettle" of refurbishing Parliament after years of delay.

The committee said there was enough information for MPs and peers to vote on a way forward before the end of this year.

The BBC understands government whips have discussed holding a debate and vote by then, but no date has been scheduled.

This vote would decide whether to proceed with up to £3bn of initial works and narrow down four current options, ahead of a final decision by 2030.

One proposed option would see MPs and peers move out of the site for up to 24 years from 2032, costing up to £15.6bn.

Another involves moving only the House of Lords out of the building, costing £39bn and taking 61 years.

Among the "critical" setbacks the committee identified were an overcomplex decision-making process and delays in acquiring a temporary home for the Lords in the nearby Queen Elizabeth II conference centre, which is owned by the government.
